newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Governor of the Bank of Indonesia Sudradjad Djiwandono said that only through improved efficiency can Indonesia's economy continue to grow at a fast rate.

Armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung has rejected calls to reopen investigations into the 1984 Tanjung Priok riots. Last Thursday more than 200 people gathered to commemorate those who died when troops opened fire on anti-government demonstrators in the port district of Jakarta. Tanjung's comments came in response to heightened calls for an investigation by Indonesia's official human rights body.

Ousted leader of the opposition Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, will submit a list of candidates to the government today for next year's parliamentary elections. The government has said it will not accept a list from her faction of the PDI which it says it does not recognise.
Indonesia's President Suharto has urged 5,500 businessmen to contribute two percent of their profits to help alleviate poverty.
